title: Input buttons need visible text
summary: An <input type="button"> has no value, so it has no name. Give it a value attribute that says what the button does.
problem: An <input> with type="button" has no value attribute, no aria-label and no title, so the button shows nothing and announces no name. Submit and reset inputs get a default name from the browser, but a plain button does not.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear only "button" and cannot tell what it does. Voice control users cannot say its name to press it. Sighted users see an empty button, unless a background image is carrying the meaning.
whyItMatters: A button with no name is a dead end for anyone who relies on assistive technology, whether it opens a menu or starts a payment. This is a failure of WCAG 4.1.2 at Level A.
steps: Find the <input type="button"> in the scan result.
Add a value attribute with short text that says what the button does, such as value="Print receipt". The browser shows this text on the button.
If the button must show only an icon, add an aria-label that describes the action instead, and keep it short.
Consider changing it to a <button> element, which lets you put text and icons inside it.
howToCheck: Select the button in the browser accessibility inspector and read its Name. An empty Name confirms the problem. The fixed button should show its text and announce the same words.
